transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my mind just isn’t holding onto things like it used to. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the words and numbers just sort of scatter on me. I can’t keep them straight.
When did you first notice your mind wasn't holding onto things like it used to?
It started about three weeks ago, I think. Pretty much after my older sister died. Since then, I’ve noticed it.
Are you having trouble remembering things that happened before your sister died?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed problems with things from before she died. It feels more like what’s been happening since then is harder for me to hold onto.
Are you having trouble learning new things since your sister died?

Yes. New things just don’t stick right now. Even something simple, like writing a note for the youth maker program, I can’t keep the words or numbers straight. It’s like they scatter before I can get them down.
Do you find it hard to focus or pay attention to things since your sister died?

Yes. I can’t keep my attention on even simple things. I’ll sit down to write a note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the numbers and words just scatter on me. I lose track of what I’m trying to say.
Do you find that your thoughts are disjointed or don't make sense to you or others lately?
I’m not sure. I don’t think my thoughts are coming out in a way that doesn’t make sense exactly. I just… I lose track sometimes, but I haven’t noticed them being disjointed like that.
Have you noticed that your thoughts seem to be disconnected or don't flow logically since your sister died?
I haven’t really noticed them being disconnected like that. I lose my place sometimes, but I don’t think my thoughts stop making sense or don’t flow logically.
Are you able to remember things from a few minutes ago, like our conversation just now?
I think so, mostly. I can remember what we’ve been talking about just now, at least the general parts. I may lose my place a little, but I don’t feel like the last few minutes are just gone.
Do you have trouble recalling things that happened earlier in the day?

Yes. I mean, not everything, but I have trouble holding onto simple things from earlier. Like I’ll sit down to write a note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the words and numbers just sort of scatter on me. I can’t keep them straight the way I used to.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you're trying to express yourself?

Yes, I do. I’ll know what I’m trying to say, but when I sit down to write even a simple note for the youth maker program, the words don’t come together right. The numbers and words sort of scatter on me, and I can’t hold onto them like I used to.
Do you also have trouble finding the right words when you're speaking, not just when you're writing?

Yes, it happens when I’m talking too. I’ll know what I mean, but the word just won’t come, or I lose the thread for a moment. It’s the same kind of thing as when I try to write that simple note for the youth maker program—the words and numbers just seem to scatter, and I can’t hold onto them like I used to.
Do you feel like you know the words you're trying to use, but they just won't come to you when you're speaking or writing?

Yes. I know what I’m trying to say, but it just won’t come out right. I came in because my mind just doesn’t seem to hold onto things anymore. Even writing a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to be able to do without thinking—the words and numbers just scatter on me.
Do you feel like the words you're trying to use are completely gone from your memory, or you just can't access them when you need them?

I don’t think the words are completely gone. It’s more like I can’t get to them when I need them. My mind just won’t hold onto things anymore. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program, something I used to do without even thinking, and the words and numbers just scatter on me.
Do you think if someone reminded you of the information you're trying to recall, you would remember it?

I think if someone prompted me, maybe I’d recognize it, yes. It’s not like it’s completely erased. It’s more that in the moment my mind just won’t hold onto it. I’ll be trying to write that simple note for the youth maker program, something I used to do easily, and the words and numbers just scatter on me.
Do you think you would be able to recall the information if you were given more time to think about it?

Sometimes, maybe, if I sit with it long enough. But even with more time, it’s hard. I’ll be trying to write something simple, like a note for the youth maker program, and the words and numbers just kind of scatter. It feels like my mind won’t hold onto them the way it used to.
Do you find it harder to remember things that involve words and language, or things that don't, like following instructions or remembering faces?

It seems worse with words and numbers, I think. Like when I sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program, something I used to do without any trouble, I just can’t keep it together. The words scatter, the numbers scatter, and my mind won’t hold onto them.
Do you have as much trouble remembering things that don't involve words, like pictures or actions, as you do with words and numbers?

Not as much, I don’t think. The main trouble is with words and numbers. I’ll sit down to write even a simple note for the youth maker program, something I used to do almost without thinking, and it just scatters on me. My mind won’t hold onto it.
Do you have trouble remembering things you've seen or done, like pictures or routines, as much as you do with words and numbers?

Not as much, no. It’s really the words and numbers that fall apart on me. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program, something I used to do without thinking, and I just can’t hold it in my mind anymore. It scatters before I can get it down.
Do you think your trouble with words and numbers is more because you can't understand or process them, or because you just can't remember them?

I think it’s more that I can’t hold onto them. I can understand the words or the numbers in the moment, but when I try to use them—like writing a simple note for the youth maker program—they just scatter. It’s like my mind won’t keep them in place long enough.
Do you think you would be able to recall something new you learned today, like a phone number, if someone asked you about it tomorrow?

I don’t think I would, not reliably. If you told me a phone number today, I might understand it right then, but by tomorrow I think it would be gone—or mixed up. That’s kind of why I came in. My mind just won’t hold onto words and numbers the way it used to.
